title: How long is the last word?
scenario: A sign painter leaves two spaces after the last word on a label. How long is the last word?

intro.job: A sign painter leaves two spaces after the last word on a label. How long is the last word?

idea.rule: Skip the trailing spaces first — the last word starts after them.
idea.detail: Walk backwards from the end with a finger, i. First, step over any spaces hanging off the end — they aren't part of any word. Only then start counting letters, and stop at the next space (or the start of the string). Two small loops, one after the other: skip, then count.

watch.code:
i = len(s) - 1
while i >= 0 and s[i] == " ":
    i -= 1
count = 0
while i >= 0 and s[i] != " ":
    count += 1
    i -= 1
print(count)

model_restatement: Find the last real word on the label — ignoring spaces at the end — and print how many letters it has.

clarify.question: What if the label is all spaces?
clarify.answer: Not today — there's always at least one word.

clarify.question: Punctuation?
clarify.answer: None today — letters and spaces only.

clarify.question: Can I use strip() and split()?
clarify.answer: In real work, yes. Here, walk the string by hand — that's the pattern.

clarify_fallback: Good question — assume the simple case.
blueprint: Start at the last character. Count characters going backwards until you hit a space. Print the count.

checkpoints.prompt: On the print line, what is count?
With the fix — after the second skipped space, what is i?

why_line: The label ends in a space, so s[i] != ' ' is False on the very first check — the counting loop never runs and count stays 0.

explain.rule: Counting back from the end without skipping the gap is measuring a parked car from the curb — the first thing you touch is empty space, so you stop at zero.
explain.bridge: What's at the very end of the label — and what has to happen before you can start counting letters?

fix.rule: Two walks back: first step over the trailing spaces, then count letters until the next space.

walk.gloss: Still on a space at the end?
Now on a letter: keep going while it's not a space...
...counting each letter of the last word.

fix.recommended:
i = len(s) - 1
while i >= 0 and s[i] == " ":
    i -= 1
count = 0
while i >= 0 and s[i] != " ":
    count += 1
    i -= 1
print(count)

alternatives.note: Strip the ends and split on any whitespace — correct, and the shortest way to say it.
